edges.description: Constitutive PDGFRB signaling activates the STAT5-IGF1 axis.
Constitutive PDGFRB activation leads to progressive arterial wall dilation and remodeling in cerebral and coronary arteries.

edges.description: Activating PDGFRB signaling in dermal connective tissues leads to hyperelastic, translucent, and fragile skin.
Gain-of-function PDGFRB signaling causes progressive wasting of subcutaneous adipose tissue.
Constitutive PDGFRB signaling is associated with progressive periventricular white matter abnormalities and neurologic decline.
Activating PDGFRB variants are associated with posterior fossa arachnoid cysts on neuroimaging through an uncharacterized developmental mechanism.
STAT5-IGF1 signaling alters skeletal stem cell fate, promoting chondrogenesis.
Promotion of chondrogenesis over osteogenesis drives generalized somatic and acral overgrowth.
Longitudinal skeletal overgrowth produces tall stature.
Skeletal overgrowth and axial dysplasia manifest with progressive scoliosis after early childhood.
Progressive craniofacial skeletal overgrowth produces coarse facial features after early childhood.
Jaw and craniofacial overgrowth is accompanied by widely spaced teeth.
Craniofacial skeletal overgrowth is associated with macrocephaly in some affected individuals.
Altered skeletal stem cell fate and defective osteogenesis produce generalized skeletal dysplasia.
Skeletal and connective-tissue involvement in KOGS manifests with progressive flexion contractures.
Acral and digital involvement in KOGS manifests with camptodactyly.
Progressive arterial wall dilation in the basilar and vertebral arteries produces cerebrovascular ectasia and fusiform aneurysms.

edges.description: Progressive arterial wall dilation in the coronary circulation produces coronary artery aneurysms.

edges.description: Dermal connective-tissue alteration manifests clinically as hyperelastic, thin, and fragile skin.
Progressive loss of subcutaneous adipose depots manifests clinically as lipodystrophy.
Cerebral white matter pathology appears on brain MRI as periventricular white matter signal abnormalities.
Progressive cerebral white matter lesions are accompanied by neurological and cognitive deterioration.
